California made SB 1168 and AB 1577 law on September 21. They are two of seven data-centre bills signed that day; this article covers only these two. Neither law gives households an immediate bill credit or proves that electricity rates will fall.

SB 1168 tells the California Public Utilities Commission to assess opportunities for rate structures — the rules used to divide charges among customer groups. The assessment must consider data centres’ reasonable share of transmission and distribution costs, their proportionate share of load and procurement costs, and pressure on residential customers.

source.passage: Governor Newsom today signed seven bills to strengthen California’s approach to data centers — requiring data centers to report about water and electricity use.

sources.limitations: Official signing announcement and chaptered text checked September 26. The story covers only these two laws.

source.passage: As part of a new or existing proceeding, the commission shall assess opportunities for rate structures to do all of the following:

sources.limitations: Chaptered SB 1168 checked September 26. The law requires an assessment inside a proceeding; no adopted tariff or savings result is supplied.

source.passage: Ensure data centers pay their reasonable share of costs associated with transmission and distribution needs, regardless of whether the data centers interconnect at the transmission or distribution level.

sources.limitations: Chaptered SB 1168 checked September 26. The law requires an assessment inside a proceeding; no adopted tariff or savings result is supplied.

source.passage: Ensure data centers pay for their proportionate share of load increases and procurements needed to reliably serve their loads while maintaining consistency with the applicable integrated resource planning requirements.

sources.limitations: Chaptered SB 1168 checked September 26. The law requires an assessment inside a proceeding; no adopted tariff or savings result is supplied.

source.passage: Alleviate cost pressures on residential ratepayers, including, but not limited to, customers enrolled in the California Alternate Rates for Energy program described in Section 739.1 and the Family Electric Rate Assistance program described in Section 739.12.

sources.limitations: Chaptered SB 1168 checked September 26. The law requires an assessment inside a proceeding; no adopted tariff or savings result is supplied.

source.passage: As part of a new or existing proceeding, the commission shall assess opportunities for rate structures to do all of the following:

sources.limitations: Bounded inference from the operative assessment duty and absence of any supplied adopted tariff or bill calculation.

source.passage: Upon applying for a discretionary permit, entitlement, or land use authorization required for the construction or operation of a data center, the owner or operator of the data center shall submit to the applicable local agency an estimate of all of the following information, to the extent applicable to the proposed facility:

sources.limitations: Chaptered AB 1577 checked September 26. The commission specifies submission manner and timing.

source.passage: The commission shall establish a process for the owner or operator of a data center to submit all of the following information to the commission upon energization of the data center and following any substantive change to information previously submitted pursuant to this paragraph:

sources.limitations: Chaptered AB 1577 checked September 26. The commission specifies submission manner and timing.

source.passage: The commission shall establish a process for the owner or operator of a data center to submit all of the following information to the commission at least annually following energization, disaggregated by month over the reporting period unless otherwise specified by the commission.

sources.limitations: Chaptered AB 1577 checked September 26. The commission specifies submission manner and timing.

source.passage: The commission shall annually publish the information submitted pursuant to subdivision (b) in an anonymized and aggregated format on its internet website.

sources.limitations: Public release is aggregate, not a promised facility-level dossier.

source.passage: Beginning with the 2029 integrated energy policy report required pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 25302, and in subsequent biennial reports required pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 25302 thereafter as determined by the commission, the commission shall include an assessment of electrical load trends for data centers.

sources.limitations: Public release is aggregate, not a promised facility-level dossier.

source.passage: “Data center” does not include a facility with an electrical capacity of less than 10 megawatts.

sources.limitations: These limits apply to the cited AB 1577 provisions, not automatically to the other five signed laws.

source.passage: This section does not apply to a publicly funded research facility, public safety facility, publicly funded national security facility, publicly owned facility, or other utility facility, including, but not limited to, a facility operated for the purpose of providing telecommunications services to the public by a terrestrial facilities-based telecommunications, cable, or internet service provider.

sources.limitations: These limits apply to the cited AB 1577 provisions, not automatically to the other five signed laws.

source.passage: The State Energy Resources Conservation and Development Commission or a local agency shall not disclose information submitted pursuant to Section 65909.3 of this code or to subdivision (b) of Section 25302.10 of the Public Resources Code in a manner that would result in the disclosure of personally identifiable information or energy consumption data for a specific data center customer.
